FAQ

Does shipping Head Tracking or head-pointer support auto-translate my China listing?

No. Head Tracking, head pointer, head-pose control, and head-driven pointer interaction are on-device accessibility or spatial input behaviors — they do not create or fill a Simplified Chinese localization row. Empty or English zh-Hans fields mean China buyers see en-US fallback even when your US listing mentions Head Tracking or 头部追踪.

How is this different from Eye Tracking or Hand Tracking listing copy?

Eye Tracking markets front-camera eye-gaze control and dwell to select with your eyes — 眼动追踪 / 注视控制. Hand Tracking markets visionOS pinch and gesture control without controllers — 手部追踪. Head Tracking markets head pose, head pointer, and head-driven pointer interaction — 头部追踪, 头控指针, 头姿控制. Head pose is not eye gaze and not hand pinch.

How is this different from Switch Control, Dwell Control, or Accessibility hub copy?

Switch Control markets adaptive-switch scanning — 切换控制. Dwell Control markets pointer-rest timing to click — 停留控制. Accessibility hub markets the broad assistive category. Head Tracking markets head pose / head pointer as the lead story — 头部追踪 — not switch scanning, not dwell timing as the hero, and not a generic Accessibility umbrella.

Paste-ready Simplified Chinese (zh-Hans) copy for App Store Connect listing fields you specify: title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text when included, and screenshot overlay or caption lines — rewritten from your English Head Tracking and head pointer / head-pose marketing originals.
